findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact surfaces in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Soda nozzle holder at the bar was soiled with mold and grime. Inspector showed bar tender and PIC. Bar tender cleaned on site - wash, rinse, sanitize. COS.
2. Pizza tray for the pizza oven was observed to be heavily soiled with burned pizza debris. 
3. Ice machine in the back room (where pizza oven is) has a thick accumulation of pink slime/mold on the interior baffle lip. Inspector showed PIC. Ensure the ice is removed and the interior of the ice machine is washed, rinsed, and sanitized.

Inspector will follow-up on 6/1/23 regarding #2 and #3. Ensure all areas above are routinely cleaned - wash, rinse, sanitize - in order to prevent mold and/or food debris build-up.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At this time, the facility is a Class-II facility. This requires a certified food protection manager (CFPM) to be present at all times. On arrival, no CFPM was at the facility. A CFPM arrived during the inspection to correct. Education took place with them in relation to the code requirements. A copy of the current available classes was given to the PIC as well as a copy of the pizza variance request paperwork.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

No reporting agreements or similar verification are available at the facility on inspector’s request. Education took place and the reporting agreements distributed by SCDPH were given to the PIC during the inspection. They are instructed to have employees sign and maintain them at the facility.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

The biohazard kit at the facility is visibly degraded in the bag and without the disinfectant. The hand out distributed by SCDPH was given to the facility and they already have bleach at the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The bars of the rack that pizzas are cooked on is observed with a thick accumulation of grease. The rack was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

The scoop used for ice is observed with the handle in contact with the ice. Education took place and the scoop was moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (A) (Pf) Refrigerated, READY-TO EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.
A container of milk that has been opened and partially used was observed in the bar cooler without a date mark. Discussion with the bartender revealed that it was opened the previous Friday (4/4/19). Inspector discussed the requirements with the bartender and a date mark was placed on the container during the inspection.
